note: RFC 4271 Section 9.2: "All newly installed routes and all newly unfeasible routes for which there is no replacement route SHALL be advertised to its peers by means of an UPDATE message." Re-judged 2026-10-26 by an independent auditor after the tags moved from plugins/rib/rfc4271_rib_bestchange_test.go (745b0890f8) to reactor/rfc4271_rs_replacement_test.go. Both carriers drive the real bgp-rs, bgp-rib and bgp-adj-rib-in over live TCP sessions and judge the client's replayed TCP history behind a causal fence taken once the client owes nothing. Positive TestRFC4271RouteServerLastSourceWithdrawalIsSent: the only source withdraws P; the client no longer holds P, saw exactly one withdrawal of P and exactly one announcement (no re-announcement), so the no-replacement clause is asserted at the wire, not as an internal event. Negative TestRFC4271RouteServerOwnerWithdrawalSendsReplacement: the owner of the held best withdraws while another source's route is retained; the client ends on the retained route's exact attributes with zero withdrawals of P, which proves both the newly installed replacement is advertised and the bare withdrawal is confined to the no-replacement case; the earlier newly-installed steps (B's route, then A's better route reaching C) are also asserted. Discrimination records verified: revert of relay_recovery.go::queueRecoveryWithdrawal reddens the positive; mutant owesWithdrawal 'entry == nil' -> true (owner withdrawal sent bare) reddens the negative. The earlier weak finding (an internal BestChangeWithdraw event, no UPDATE, no newly-installed carrier) is answered by the new units. Scope read: owesWithdrawal/oweAnnouncement (session_ownership.go) and recoveryOwedFor (recovery_owed.go) do not branch on RSClient, so the RS-client fixture exercises the general non-ADD-PATH path; when the RIB recovery owner is not attached to the source, the bare withdrawal is sent with a warning naming the attach fix (ownerReceives), a misconfiguration path no tag covers.
